key_facts: Earth's lithosphere comprises a number of large tectonic plates, which have been slowly moving since 3–4 billion years ago
Plate tectonics came to be accepted by geoscientists after seafloor spreading was validated in the mid- to late 1960s
fractured into seven or eight major plates (depending on how they are defined) and many minor plates or "platelets"
The relative movement of the plates typically ranges from zero to 10 cm annually
Jupiter's moon Europa shows signs of ice crustal plates moving and interacting
Average oceanic lithosphere is typically 100 km (62 mi) thick
Continental lithosphere is typically about 200 km (120 mi) thick
The San Andreas Fault in California is an example of a transform boundary exhibiting dextral motion

forbidden_claims.claim: Tectonic plates typically move up to 500 centimeters annually.
Mars today has stronger, ongoing plate tectonics than Earth does.
The Ring of Fire mostly circles the Arctic Ocean's plate boundaries.

notes: Earth is explicitly the only planet with CURRENT active tectonics; Mars/Venus are past-tense -- a reversal trap.
